lists.content:
• Manage 3–4 other designers, and part-time contributors
  • Define and own strategy across our website and data products 
  • Establish design processes and quality standards for the organization 
  • Lead design projects end-to-end, from problem definition through delivery
  • Design responsive user interfaces and graphs 
  • Conduct user research to help us understand audience interests and how they use our research
  • Create design specifications, mock-ups, and prototypes while contributing to our design library

• 5+ years of experience designing interactive digital products, including leading projects
  • Experience managing a team of designers
  • Fluency in interpreting data visualizations and statistical insights, to communicate topics in AI to non-expert audiences
  • A portfolio demonstrating experience in UI/UX and data visualization
  • Ability to work independently, set priorities, and lead design work in a fast-paced environment
  • Strong grasp of typography, color, and layout 
  • Ability to work comfortably in Figma, including auto-layout and components
  • Experience establishing or maintaining a design system
  • Prior familiarity with Epoch AI’s work

• Experience with scientific communication
  • Experience in illustration, branding
  • Familiarity with front-end development, HTML + CSS + JS
  • Experience with Python libraries like Matplotlib/Plotly or other data visualization programming tools
  • Good written communication skills

    • If you don’t tick all these boxes but think you would be a great fit, please consider applying anyway!

• Annual salary between $150,000–$220,000 USD, depending on location and experience. 
  • Salaries are not restricted to USD, and contracts and payments are usually in local currencies. Conversions are based on one-year average exchange rates. 
  • Remote environment, including flexible work hours. 
  • Competitive global benefits program, including a comprehensive health insurance program—including supplemental benefits specific to a local country, as available and mandated by local law—and life insurance and a pension plan, if applicable in your country. 
  • Generous paid time off (PTO), including no specific limit on PTO with 30 days per year protected, unlimited personal and sick leave, and 4 months paid parental leave for permanent staff with at least 12 months of tenure (prorated parental leave if less than 12 months). 
  • A flexible and generous expense policy for you to spend on equipment and a large range of productivity tools or learning/development opportunities you might find valuable, subject to regulations and manager approval. 
  • Access to our very well-equipped offices in Berkeley, California, including paid meals and a gym, or reimbursement for coworking space in your area, if desired.

We're seeking expressions of interest for Special Projects Associate roles, where you'll provide specialized operations support for our research teams. 
Note: We are characterizing this opening as an expression of interest because we are not actively prioritizing filling this role at this time. However, we are excited to hear from candidates whose skills and interests are exceptionally aligned with our organizational needs. We're open to working with promising candidates to clarify the scope and responsibilities of the role in a way that plays to their strengths and interests. 
About the role
We are looking for a Special Projects Associate to support our research programs. Specific responsibilities will evolve as our teams launch new initiatives. In this role, you would take on a wide variety of tasks involving complex logistics to help ensure new projects can start strong and run smoothly.
Depending on organizational needs and your strengths, your work might include:
Coordinating with external experts and contractors across a wide variety of domains, ensuring their contributions meet our quality standards and improving their experience working with us.
Supporting our data projects, such as helping the data team properly secure and license data for our data center tracking and ensuring we remain compliant.
Organizing events, such as symposiums that bring together field experts.
Owning external communications channels, such as inboxes for queries from our audience, responding or triaging with the team as necessary.
Providing operational support for new research initiatives, learning about and handling the dozens of tasks and details that help make new projects great.
This role is fully remote, and we are able to hire in many countries. Depending on the team, we may require candidates to be based in certain ranges of timezones. We invite anyone who is interested to apply, regardless of background, experience, or credentials. Please do not include a cover letter, photograph, or headshot of yourself, or any personal information that is not relevant to the role for which you're applying.

descriptionPlain:
Epoch AI is looking for a Product Manager for our website, the place where most people encounter our research. You'll decide what gets built and make sure it ships well.
About the role
The website is Epoch's main product. We’re looking for someone to be responsible for what we build, what each page is for, what gets done first, and whether it's ready to go out.
Much of the job is holding the context that individual researchers do not: what our publications and data products have in common, how they relate to each other, and how we want people to use the site. You will also own the parts of the site that cut across several pieces of research, such as topic pages and the navigation.
You'd work most closely with three teams. The senior product designer and the design team turn specs into designs and own the visuals. Web developers build them. The comms team owns the writing: publications, social media, and SEO. How reports and data insights look and how they sit on the site is yours.
You’ll report directly to our COO, as does the senior product designer. For now, this is an individual contributor role without direct reports.
This role is fully remote, and we can offer contracts in many countries, though we require at least three hours of overlap in work hours with Pacific Time. We invite anyone who is interested to apply, regardless of background, experience, or credentials. Please do not include a cover letter, photograph, or headshot of yourself, or any personal information that is not relevant to the role for which you're applying (including marital status, age, identity traits, etc.). Applications are rolling.

lists.content:
• Set the goals and specs for each new page or feature with the researcher and the designer: who it is for, what it should do, what goes on it and roughly in what order.
  • Prioritize across the whole site, with the audience and usability in mind, and say no or not yet when a request does not fit.
  • Set the standards every new page follows (layout, how filters and charts work, what we call things), and decide what the shared parts of the site are for, such as who the homepage serves and what they should find there in ten seconds.
  • Run projects from goal to launch: agree the goal and spec before design starts, get the people who will use the page to review the design before it is built, make sure developers have what they need, and decide when it ships.
  • Give feedback on designs as they come, and answer designers' and developers' questions, or find the researcher who can.
  • Know the audience: use analytics, the feedback form and interviews with our user panel to decide what to build and what to cut.
  • Own QA: click through every page before it goes live and catch broken tiles, mismatched titles and menu labels, and buttons that do not do what they say, before readers do.

• Strong product taste: you can tell what our audience will find clear and what they will find cluttered or confusing before the analytics tell you, you know what to leave out, and you can explain why.
  • Clear writing: most of this job is one-page briefs, decision notes and Slack messages that busy researchers will actually read.
  • Comfort with data, charts and research: you can read a scatter plot and say what the point is, notice when a number is meaningless without context, and get up to speed on a research area fast enough to ask the right questions.
  • An understanding of our audience (policy people, journalists, researchers and people at AI labs) and how they differ from us.
  • Experience shipping web products with designers and developers, and a sense of where projects usually go wrong.
  • People skills: sometimes you'll need to tell a senior researcher that their feature is not getting built this quarter, explain why, and keep working well with them, and to change the plan when their argument is better than yours.
  • Organization: you keep track of what was decided and by whom, and you follow up.
  • Ability to travel: attendance at our three annual team retreats is expected for all staff.

• Familiarity with Epoch's research, or with AI more broadly.
  • Prior product management experience, in tech, on a website, or at a research organization or newsroom.
  • Enough front-end knowledge to have a sensible conversation with developers about what is easy and what is hard.
  • Comfort with AI coding tools. Our researchers and developers use Claude to change the site directly, and part of this job is keeping that fast without the site becoming incoherent.
    • If you don't tick all these boxes but think you would be a great fit, please consider applying anyway!

• Annual salary between $115,000 and $185,000 USD, depending on location and experience.
  • For successful candidates based in the San Francisco Bay Area, we will adjust salaries upwards to 21% more.
  • In Washington DC and New York City, we will adjust salaries upwards to 10% more.
  • In countries where employment costs are particularly high we will adjust salaries downwards 10%, or 20% in Brazil, Sweden, or France. 
  • Salaries are not restricted to USD, and contracts and payments are usually in local currencies. Conversions are based on one-year average exchange rates.
  • Fully remote environment if desired, including flexible work hours.
  • Competitive global benefits program, including a comprehensive health insurance program—including supplemental benefits specific to a local country, as available and mandated by local law—and life insurance and a pension plan, if applicable in your country.
  • Generous paid time off (PTO), including no specific annual limit, with 30 days PTO per year protected, unlimited personal and sick leave, and 4 months paid parental leave for permanent staff with at least 12 months of tenure (prorated parental leave if less than 12 months).
  • A flexible and generous expense policy for you to spend on equipment and a large range of productivity tools or learning/development opportunities, including unlimited spending on AI tools, subject to regulations and manager approval.
  • Access to our very well-equipped offices in Berkeley, California, including paid meals and a gym, or reimbursement for coworking space in your area, if desired.

description: Epoch AI is seeking researchers and senior researchers to improve society's understanding of AI capabilities and their trajectories.

lists.content:
Epoch researchers examine the driving forces behind AI, track the progress of AI capabilities, and measure and forecast its impact. They help define future research directions and open new investigations into trends that matter. Eight teams are currently hiring researchers and senior researchers, descriptions below.

We are a fully remote organization, and we’re able to hire in many countries from Pacific Time to Central European Time. We invite anyone who is interested to apply, regardless of background, experience, or credentials. Please do not include a cover letter, photograph, or headshot of yourself, or any personal information that is not relevant to the role for which you're applying (including marital status, age, identity traits, etc.). The researcher/senior researcher role will remain open, as we’re always looking for exceptional people to join our teams.

• Data Center Team
    Data center researchers will produce data insights and reports about frontier AI data centers, and improve the methodology behind the AI Data Centers explorer. Potential research topics include the data center buildout across countries, constraints to the buildout, and estimating the kind of chips inside different data centers. Depending on fit, the role may include managing contractors who analyze individual data centers.

  • Supply Chain Team
    Supply chain researchers will investigate the supply chain for compute and other AI inputs. From components to owners, where are all the chips in the world, who is using them and how are they being paid for? What is the trajectory for the future? Outputs include data explorers, data insights, and reports.

  • Polling & Experiments Team
    Polling and experiments researchers will design and analyze polls, RCTs, and other behavioral data on AI usage. Their work will investigate the impacts of AI, uplift, and the strategic landscape of AI.

• Special Projects Team
    Special projects researchers will run self-contained exploratory investigations into new questions for Epoch, publishing the results as reports or newsletter posts. The most promising directions may later be developed by other teams into lasting products. Examples of past and current topics include: what job listings reveal about frontier labs, how quickly robot production could scale, indicators for how much AI R&D has been automated, estimates of the amount and cost of available training data, and whether we can detect that a model was distilled from another.

  • Gradient Updates Team
    Researchers for Gradient Updates will focus on analyzing big-picture questions about AI progress and its societal impacts, e.g. understanding the factors that impact the chances of rapid recursive self-improvement, what compute constraints mean for US-China AI competition, and the future of AI benchmarks. They will then write up their findings and share them broadly via Epoch's newsletter, to help inform discourse and key decision-making about the future of AI.

• Benchmarking Team
    Benchmarking researchers will create, run, and analyze benchmarks that measure important AI capabilities. Our benchmarks focus on areas of economic import as well as capabilities pertaining to highly impactful dynamics, like recursive self-improvement. Areas where we are excited to build benchmarking include: AI R&D, general mathematical and scientific discovery, long horizon strategic reasoning, cybersecurity, computer use, and multimodal/spatial reasoning.

  • Benchmarking Reviews Team
    Benchmark reviewers will work on a new project to review and certify benchmarks. This will involve researching individual benchmark quality and public writeups of the results. The role may also expand to include writing guides for benchmark development, and there is flexibility to spend some time on direct benchmark development.

  • Epoch Capabilities Index (ECI) and Capability Trends Team
    ECI and capability trends researchers will work on maintaining, improving, and extending the ECI and other projects to better understand model capabilities and trends. Examples of potential projects include extending our analysis of trend breaks, incorporating inference compute into scaling laws, or running experiments on AI models. Statistics background useful but not required.

While each team has specific skills and experience in mind, we value these skills in particular across the board: 

  • Curiosity and learning speed. You rapidly absorb new information across diverse domains and stay at the forefront of a fast-moving field. You seek out new research and enjoy diving into unfamiliar topics.

  • Rigorous reasoning under uncertainty. You make quantitative estimates with limited information and reason clearly about uncertainty.

  • Familiarity with AI trends. 

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills. 

  • Outstanding candidates might have prior experience in research areas similar to Epoch’s field; experience in at least one part of the AI development pipeline (hardware, datacenters, benchmarks, etc.); or relevant experience in related organizations. 

    • If you don’t tick all these boxes but think you would be a great fit, please consider applying anyway!

• Researcher: annual salary between $115,000 and $185,000 USD. Senior Researcher: annual salary between $168,000 and $300,000 USD. Exact salaries depend on seniority and location. We are willing to pay above these ranges for exceptional candidates in key locations.

  • Salaries are not restricted to USD, and contracts and payments are usually in local currencies. Conversions are based on one-year average exchange rates.

  • Fully remote environment, including flexible work hours and schedules for most roles; paid access to local coworking space as desired. 

  • Competitive global benefits program, including a comprehensive health insurance program—including supplemental benefits specific to a local country, as available and mandated by local law—and life insurance and a pension plan, if applicable in your country.

  • Generous paid time off (PTO), including no specific annual limit, with 30 days PTO per year protected, unlimited personal and sick leave, and 4 months paid parental leave for permanent staff with at least 12 months of tenure (prorated parental leave if less than 12 months). 

  • A flexible and generous expense policy for you to spend on equipment and a large range of productivity tools or learning/development opportunities you might find valuable, subject to regulations and manager approval.

  • Access to our very well-equipped offices in Berkeley, California, including paid meals, snacks, gym, and more.

While we welcome applicants from all time zones, we prefer candidates who can overlap with UTC–8 (Pacific Time) and UTC (Greenwich Mean Time), as most of our staff work in this range of time zones. We also prefer candidates who can travel: we hold three retreats per year. 

Please submit all of your application materials in English and note that we require professional level English proficiency.

Epoch is committed to building an inclusive, equitable, and supportive community for you to thrive and do your best work. We’re committed to finding the best people for our team, so please don’t hesitate to apply for a role regardless of your age, gender identity/expression, political identity, personal preferences, physical abilities, veteran status, neurodiversity or any other background. Please email careers@epoch.ai if you have any questions about this role, accessibility requests, or if you want to request an extension to the application deadline. However, we will not review applications submitted to this email address; please submit your application through the link on this page.

Epoch AI is a research institute that investigates trends in machine learning and the economic consequences of AI. Our mission is to develop a comprehensive, publicly accessible knowledge base on AI that informs policymakers, industry leaders, and society at large.

We strive to achieve both rigor and accessibility to our work, as exemplified by some of our most successful projects, including our database of AI models and our AI trends dashboard. Our body of research includes our work on compute trends (IJCN 2022), data scarcity (ICML 2024), and algorithmic progress (NeurIPS 2024). You can read more about our work and mission on our website and in this Time profile.

  • Expertise running social media accounts on X, Substack, and LinkedIn as well as Instagram and TikTok
  • Based in the San Francisco Bay Area, or willing to relocate, and able to work in person with the team

    • If you don’t tick all these boxes but think you would be a great fit, please consider applying anyway!

• Annual salary between $115,000 and $125,000 USD, or more for exceptional candidates.
  • For successful candidates based in the San Francisco Bay Area, we will adjust salaries upwards to 21% more.
  • In Washington DC and New York City, we will adjust salaries upwards to 10% more.
  • In countries where employment costs are particularly high we will adjust salaries downwards 10%, or 20% in Brazil, Sweden, or France.
  • Salaries are not restricted to USD, and contracts and payments are usually in local currencies. Conversions are based on one-year average exchange rates.
  • The opportunity to help build a new media team from the ground up, meaningfully shape its direction and share in the upside.
  • Competitive benefits program, including comprehensive health insurance, life insurance, and a retirement plan.
  • Generous paid time off (PTO), including no specific annual limit, with 30 days PTO per year protected, unlimited personal and sick leave, and 4 months paid parental leave for permanent staff with at least 12 months of tenure (prorated parental leave if less than 12 months). 
  • A flexible and generous expense policy for you to spend on equipment and a large range of productivity tools or learning/development opportunities, including unlimited spending on AI tools, subject to regulations and manager approval. 
  • Optional paid work trips, such as relevant conferences.
  • A desk at our very well-equipped offices in Berkeley, California, including paid meals, snacks, gym, and more.

descriptionBody:
Epoch AI is looking for a founding Social Video Producer who will help us launch short-form video for our new media program. The role will involve producing and editing videos about AI for TikTok and Instagram, and shaping how we show up on those platforms. 

About the role

We are looking for a Social Video Producer to help us bring Epoch AI's research to a much broader audience. You will work closely with our media program lead to build our short-form video presence from scratch, aiming for roughly one video per week to start.

Your day-to-day activities will include producing and editing short-form videos, developing repeatable formats, and advising on our social strategy (what to post, when, and how to grow engagement). An ideal candidate is a strong video producer first; deep AI knowledge is not required, since the point of this program is to reach people who don't follow AI closely. Your work will be key to making rigorous AI research accessible to a general audience. 

We have a strong preference for candidates who are able to work in-person in our Berkeley office, particularly during the first six months as the media team gets established. We can hire in many countries, though we require working hours that overlap with Pacific Time for at least 4 hours during the workday.

We invite anyone who is interested to apply, regardless of background, experience, or credentials. Please do not include a cover letter, photograph, or headshot of yourself, or any personal information that is not relevant to the role for which you're applying (including marital status, age, identity traits, etc.). Applications are rolling.
